subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 24-year-old man presents with 2 weeks of cough productive of blood-streaked sputum, progressive dyspnea, and dark, smoky urine. He smokes one pack per day. Blood pressure is 148/92 mm Hg, creatinine is 2.9 mg/dL, and urinalysis shows red blood cell casts and proteinuria. Serology is positive for anti-glomerular basement membrane antibodies.
question: Which of the following best explains the combination of pulmonary hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis in this patient?

options.text: Autoantibodies bind type IV collagen present in both alveolar and glomerular basement membranes
Circulating immune complexes containing streptococcal antigens deposit in both capillary beds
Antinuclear antibodies cross-react with pulmonary and renal endothelial cells
Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies cause a small-vessel vasculitis of the lung and kidney
Amyloid fibrils deposit along both the alveolar and glomerular basement membranes

explanation_correct: This patient has Goodpasture syndrome, in which autoantibodies are directed against the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen, a component of basement membranes. Because the same antigen is present in both the alveolar and glomerular basement membranes, the antibodies bind both sites and produce pulmonary hemorrhage together with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. Smoking is a classic trigger that increases alveolar capillary permeability and exposes the antigen in the lung.

explanation_incorrect.B: Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis causes immune complex deposition in the glomerulus but does not produce diffuse alveolar hemorrhage.
explanation_incorrect.C: Antinuclear antibodies occur in systemic lupus erythematosus, which can cause both lung and kidney disease, but this patient's specific anti-GBM antibodies indicate Goodpasture syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.D: ANCA-associated vasculitis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis, microscopic polyangiitis) can cause pulmonary-renal syndrome, but it is a vasculitis rather than antibody binding to basement membrane collagen, and ANCA would be the relevant serology.
explanation_incorrect.E: Amyloidosis produces proteinuria and can affect many organs, but it does not present as acute pulmonary hemorrhage with anti-GBM antibodies.

educationalObjective: Goodpasture syndrome is caused by autoantibodies against type IV collagen shared by alveolar and glomerular basement membranes, producing pulmonary hemorrhage and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis.
